title: State management
literature: GoF State/Memento; Nystrom (state machines, snapshot); Fowler event sourcing; state-management UI (flux/redux lineage); immutable state idioms.

members.name: Aggregate
members.what: A cluster of associated objects treated as a single unit for data changes, with one root entity through which all external references and modifications must pass.

members.name: Behavior Tree
members.what: AI decision logic is structured as a tree of composable nodes (sequence, selector/fallback, parallel, decorators, leaf tasks) evaluated by periodic ticks that return success/failure/running, giving reactive hierarchical behavior without exp

members.name: Client-Side Prediction
members.what: The client applies its own inputs to a locally predicted copy of authoritative state immediately, tags each input with a sequence number, and on receiving authoritative server state rewinds to it and replays still-unacknowledged inputs.

members.name: Collections for States
members.what: Objects are placed in per-state collections; an object's state is encoded by which collection currently holds it, and state transitions move it between collections.

members.name: Context Object
members.what: Execution-scoped state (security principal, transaction, locale, request data) is bundled into one context object passed along the processing path instead of via globals or long parameter lists.

members.name: Data Binding
members.what: Declaratively connects a UI element's displayed value to a data source so changes propagate automatically instead of via hand-written synchronization code.

members.name: Dead Reckoning
members.what: Each node extrapolates remote entities' current state from their last received kinematic update (position, velocity, acceleration) via an agreed model, and senders transmit a new update only when their real state diverges from the shared mo

members.name: Decomposed AND-State
members.what: Implementing a statechart's concurrent (AND) regions by decomposing them into separate coordinated state machine objects, each handling its region's events.

members.name: Deferred Event
members.what: Events that arrive at an inconvenient state are set aside in a deferral queue and recalled for processing when the machine reaches a state that can handle them.

members.name: Deterministic Lockstep
members.what: Peers run bit-identical deterministic simulations from the same seed and exchange only per-tick inputs; each side advances a tick only once all participants' inputs for that tick have arrived.

members.name: Dirty Checking
members.what: Detects state changes by re-evaluating watched expressions and comparing new values against stored previous values in a check loop (repeated until stable), rather than by intercepting writes.

members.name: Dirty Flag
members.what: Track whether derived data is out of sync with its primary source using a boolean flag, and recompute the derived data only when it is both dirty and needed.

members.name: Dirty Rectangles
members.what: Track the screen regions modified since the last frame and redraw or recomposite only those rectangles instead of the whole display.

members.name: Finite State Machine
members.what: Behavior modeled as a finite set of states, events, and transitions, where the reaction to an event depends on the current state.

members.name: Hierarchical State Machine
members.what: A state machine extended with nested states (behavioral inheritance of transitions from enclosing states), orthogonal regions, and history, per Harel's statechart formalism.

members.name: Hydration
members.what: Attaches client-side behavior (event listeners, component state) to server-rendered static markup by re-running component logic and adopting the existing DOM instead of re-creating it.

members.name: Immutable Value
members.what: Value objects are made unmodifiable after construction, so they can be freely shared and aliased - including across threads - without copying or locking.

members.name: Interior Mutability
members.what: Types like Cell/RefCell/Mutex allow controlled mutation through shared (immutable) references by moving aliasing checks to runtime or hardware.

members.name: Lag Compensation
members.what: The server keeps a short history of world state and, when processing a client's time-stamped action, temporarily rewinds targets to where the acting client saw them at the moment of the action before adjudicating it.

members.name: Methods for States
members.what: Modal behavior is realized by swapping function/method references (or delegates) as the mode changes, so dispatch selects the current mode's behavior without conditionals.

members.name: Multiple Event Receptor
members.what: A state machine implementation exposing one function per event type, each dispatching internally on the current state.

members.name: Optimistic UI Update
members.what: Applies the expected result of a user action to local UI state immediately, before server confirmation, then reconciles with the authoritative response - rolling back if the operation fails.

members.name: Orthogonal Component
members.what: Independent concurrent behaviors are implemented as separate state-machine components contained by (and exchanging events with) a container machine, instead of as orthogonal regions of one chart.

members.name: Signals (fine-grained reactivity)
members.what: State cells that automatically track which computations read them and re-run exactly those computations (computeds/effects) when the cell changes, giving fine-grained dependency-graph updates without diffing.

members.name: Reminder
members.what: The state machine posts an event to itself to convert an internal condition into an explicit event that triggers further transitions.

members.name: Rollback Netcode
members.what: Peers advance a deterministic simulation without waiting for remote inputs by predicting them; when actual remote inputs arrive and differ from the prediction, the engine restores a saved earlier state and re-simulates the intervening frame

members.name: Rules Engine
members.what: A component that evaluates a collection of independent condition-action (production) rules against working state, with the engine — not imperative code order — deciding which rules fire, including chaining when one rule's action changes ano

members.name: Run-to-Completion Event Processing
members.what: Each event is processed fully - all transitions, entry/exit actions - before the next event is dequeued, so the machine is never observed mid-transition.

members.name: Single Event Receptor
members.what: A state machine implementation exposing one event-receptor function that takes a parameterized event object and dispatches on current state and event type (synchronously or via a queue).

members.name: State Transition Table
members.what: The state machine's transitions are encoded as a state x event table of handler/next-state entries, and a generic engine indexes the table to dispatch events.

members.name: Transition to History
members.what: The most recently active substate of a composite state is recorded on exit so a later transition can return to where the machine left off rather than to the default initial substate.

members.name: Ultimate Hook
members.what: A composite (super)state provides default event handling that nested substates inherit and may selectively override, mirroring how a GUI framework's default window procedure works.

members.name: Undo/Redo Command Stack
members.what: Records executed operations as command objects (with state backups or inverse operations) on a history stack, so popping replays/reverts them to implement undo and redo.
